_comment: Tier-2 for skfem wave#6, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / meshio 5.3.5. Claim: meshio needs 3D points so a 2D mesh must be z-padded, signalled by meshio.write raising WriteError, and a wrong cell-type tag 'produces a silently malformed .vtu file'. Ran: meshio.write of a 4x4 MeshQuad with raw (16,2) points, then five cell tags (quad, triangle, quad8, line, tetra) on the same 9x4 connectivity, each written and read back. Printed: BOTH HALVES POINT THE WRONG WAY. 2D points raise NOTHING -- the file is written, reads back with a (16,3) point array whose third column meshio supplied as zeros, and the only notice is plain text on the process stdout ('Warning: VTU requires 3D points, but 2D points given.') that is not a Python warning (empty catch_warnings record) and escapes contextlib.redirect_stdout. A wrong tag USUALLY RAISES: triangle, quad8 and line all raise WriteError naming the expected nodes-per-cell. THE GENUINELY SILENT MIS-TAG is one with the same node count -- tagging 4-node quads as 'tetra' passes meshio's only check, writes without a murmur, and reads back as tetrahedra on a mesh whose z-coordinates are all zero.
expect_in_output: VTU requires 3D points, but 2D points given
